explanation: The French north is Saint-Martin and the Dutch south is Sint Maarten, a country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands. Visitors cross between them freely.

claims.text: The island of Saint Martin is divided between France and the Kingdom of the Netherlands.
The United Kingdom, Spain and Denmark hold no part of Saint Martin.
The northern, French part of the island is called Saint-Martin and the southern, Dutch part is called Sint Maarten.
Sint Maarten is a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.
People can cross between the French and Dutch parts of Saint Martin without border checks.

evidence.restatement: Only France and the Netherlands (via Sint Maarten) hold parts of Saint Martin.
The north is the French collectivity of Saint-Martin and the south is Sint Maarten.
Sint Maarten has been a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands since 2010.
There are no border controls between the French and Dutch parts of the island.

issues.note: The key is 'Netherlands'. Strictly the southern half is Sint Maarten, a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, not part of the European Netherlands. The usual phrasing is 'France and the Netherlands' and no option is closer, so there is no second answer, and the explanation spells it out. No change needed.
